newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks end lower on selective forced selling.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks end lower on selective forced selling.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed lower, pressured by forced selling in selected stocks following recent heavy buying, dealers said.

"There's heavy forced selling in selected stocks which is expected after the fall in recent days," said William Chan, an institutional dealer at Seagroatt & Campbell. "The market is also worried about possible hike in U.S. interest rates."
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended down 0.61 of a point at 1,249.72. The small-capitalised Second Board index was down 7.77 points or 1.17 percent to 654.73.
Market volume was 560 million shares, against 552 million on Tuesday. Decliners led advancers 496 to 152.
"The selling should clear in a day or two and prices should stabilise," Chan said.
Leading the fall was Yaohan Holdings which dropped 2.50 ringgit to 12.40 ringgit.
Shangri-La Hotels was among the most active stocks, on rumours Landmarks Holdings may be looking to sell its stake in the hotel group.
Shangri-La stock rose two cents to 3.36 ringgit, while Landmarks was down two cents to 4.36.
